Data Structure
description: Do the metadata provide sufficient information about data format, data organization, features, and technical specs?

title: Data Format: File format(s) that encode the data
description: E.g.: Tabular / delimited text (CSV, TSV, XLSX, etc.) | Parquet/Arrow | JSON/JSONL | JPG/PNG/WebP/TIFF (etc.) | Non-geospatial array-based scientific data container (NetCDF, HDF5, Zarr, etc.) | Georeferenced raster data (GeoTIFF, COG, GRIB, NetCDF, Zarr, etc.) | Georeferenced vector data (points, lines, polygons; GeoPackage, GeoJSON, Shapefile, etc.) | WAV/FLAC/MP3 (etc.) | MP4/MKV (etc.) | Database file (embedded, e.g. SQLite)

title: Data Format: The dataset layout pattern
description: E.g.: Single file | Many independent files | Partitioned dataset (by year, region, taxon, etc.) | Database file | Mixed

title: Data Format: The primary unit of data that is to be operated on
description: E.g., 'Each row is a species observation'; 'Each file is a satellite image'.

title: Features or attributes are properly documented in the metadata
description: E.g., Fields for species name, location, date, observer ID, etc.

title: Features or attributes are included for each data instance
description: E.g., Each image or record (in tabular data) have complete metadata

title: Technical Specifications: What are the technical specifications of the dataset?
description: Include file sizes, total dataset size, resolution, bit depth, sampling rate, etc.

Data Origin
description: Do the metadata sufficiently capture information about the collection, instrumentation, methods, and annotation. NOTE data preparation is covered in the next section.

title: Collection (Data Source Type): Metadata record what type(s) of source data were collected or used to generate this dataset.
description: E.g.: Field observations or surveys by humans | Sensor-based data collection | Specimens, samples, and lab results | Derived or processed data

title: Collection (Curation Rationale):  Metadata record what was the primary rationale for curating or assembling this dataset
description: E.g.: Consolidate distributed sources into a unified dataset | Create ML-ready structure for AI/analytics | Improve data quality (cleaning, normalization, deduplication) | Enhance discoverability/interoperability

title: Collection (Part of a Larger Collection): Metadata indicate if this dataset part of a larger collection or series, and provide the following information:
description: Collection/series name | Persistent identifier | Relationship (IsPartOf, HasPart, IsPublishedIn) | Catalog or repository name

title: Instrumentation: Do the metadata describe the instruments or sensors used to collect the data, including their specifications and configuration.
description: E.g.: Instrument/sensor name and model | Manufacturer Sensor type (e.g., microphone, camera, spectrometer) | Key technical specs (resolution, sampling rate, spectral range, dynamic range) | Deployment/operational configuration (height, orientation, settings) | Calibration procedures | Applicable to: bioacoustics, remote sensing, environmental sensors, imaging, lab equipment, etc.

title: Methods (Collection Method Documentation): Do the metadata describe the methods used to collect or generate the data.
description: E.g.: Field, laboratory, computational, or remote sensing protocols | SOPs, manuals, workflow documents | Genetic, acoustic, imaging, trait measurement, or phylogenetic inference procedures | Links (URL/DOI) to method documentation | Deviations or customizations compared to standard methods

title: Methods (Spatial Resolution): Do the metadata describe the spatial resolution?
description: E.g.: Point location (single coordinates) | Plot/transect/area-based, grid-based | Pixel-based (remote sensing) | Voxel/3D resolution (LiDAR) | or if the data are not spatially explicit

title: Methods (Spatial Extent): Do the metadata describe the geographic coverage (region, bounding box, domain)
Methods (Temporal Resolution): Do the metadata describe the temporal resolution?
description: E.g.: Instantaneous / event-based | High-frequency (sub-second, acoustics, accelerometers) | Hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal | Annual | Continuous / streaming | Not time-explicit

title: Methods (Temporal Extent): Do the metadata describe the temporal extent?
description: E.g.: Start date End date (or leave blank if ongoing) | Optional description (e.g., seasonal sampling 2010-2024)

title: Annotation Types: Do the metadata describe the types of annotations or labels are included in the dataset (if any)?
description: E.g.: Categorical labels (e.g. species names or class IDs) | Spatial annotations (e.g. bounding boxes, segmentation masks) | Textual descriptors or tags | No annotations

title: Annotation Process: Do the metadata describe how annotations were generated or obtained?
description: E.g.: Manually by domain experts | Crowdsourced by volunteers | Automatically by an algorithm or sensor | Mixed (human-reviewed automation) | Not applicable (no annotations)

title: Annotators (Contributors): Do metadata indicate who performed the data annotations? If available, provide a list of annotators (e.g., ORCiDs), or names/versions of automated tools or systems; or other relevant information.

Data Processing
description: Do the metadata provide sufficient information about data preparation, such as correction/Standardization of values, Gaps filled, Labeling/re-labeling, Outlier removal, Splits?

title: Preparation: Do the metadata provide a complete overall description of data preparation, cleaning, transformation, or quality-control steps performed prior to generating the final dataset.
description: E.g.: Filtering, trimming, or excluding records | Merging or harmonizing multiple data sources | Manual corrections or expert verification | Gap filling, imputation, normalization | Feature engineering or deriving new variables | Conversion of raw formats (e.g., raw sensor - calibrated values) | Acoustic filtering, image preprocessing, sequence cleaning, trait standardization | Software tools, scripts, or pipelines used (with links if available)

title: Processing Platform or Software: Metadata provide a description of and citations or links to any processing platform or software used in the creation of this dataset.
Correction / Standardization of Values: Does the metadata describe corrections applied to existing data values and whether the data values have been standardized in any way?
description: E.g., Data gridding (e.g., interpolation) | Unit consistency (e.g., all in metric) | Data anonymization (removing personal IDs) | Standardizing categorical codes | Standardizing image dimensions/color spaces

title: Gaps Filled: Does metadata indicate if missing values or data gaps filled in the dataset?
If gaps were filled, are the methods described?
description: Include interpolation, imputation, or model-based gap-filling approaches.

title: Labeling / Relabeling: Does the metadata indicate if any labeling or relabeling steps applied to the dataset?
Does the metadata sufficiently describe the labeling or relabeling process.
description: Including label sources, standardization methods, and alignment with external taxonomies or ontologies.

title: Data Filtering and Outlier Removal: Were any outlier removal or filtering procedures applied to the dataset?
If yes, does the metadata sufficiently describe the outlier detection and removal methods used.
description: Including statistical thresholds, manual review, or algorithmic approaches for outlier removal.

title: Splits: Do metadata indicate if the dataset has been split into training, validation, and/or test sets?
description: E.g.: Predefined splits provided | Users define their own splits | Not applicable

title: Splits: Do the metadata provide information on how splits were created?
description: E.g.: Random, stratified, temporal, their proportions, and how data leakage was avoided.

Data Quality
description: Completeness, Consistency, Integrity, Timeliness

title: Completeness
description: The breadth of a dataset compared to an ideal 100% completion (spatial, temporal, demographic, etc.); important in avoiding bias

title: Do the metadata indicate if this dataset is complete (i.e., there are no plans for further updates to this data product)?
Have quality assurance checks been run and have they passed?
Timeliness
description: The speed of data release, compared to when an event occurred or measurements were made; requirements will vary depending on the timeframe of the phenomenon (e.g., severe thunderstorms vs. climate change, or disease outbreaks vs. life expectancy trends)

title: Do the metadata describe the timeliness of the dataset?
description: E.g: Real-time or near real-time | Periodically updated | Static (not updated) | Historical archive | Other

title: Do the metadata indicate quality checks on or evaluate dataset timeliness?
description: E.g.: Were plant surveys conducted at a time of year that makes sense given the objective of the study?

title: Describe the time lag between data collection and availability.
description: E.g., 'published within 24 hours of collection' or 'released annually'.

title: Quality Assurance Issues
description: This should also be documented under Guidance and Recommendations.

title: Do the metadata describe the quality checks that have failed and provide context for downstream users to work with the data as-is or resolve the issues.
Quality Assurance checks not performed
description: This should also be documented under Guidance and Recommendations.

title: Do the metadata explain why quality checks were not performed and provide context for downstream users to work with the data as-is or resolve potential issues.
Do the metadata  any known gaps or limitations in the dataset’s completeness.
description: Include known spatial, temporal, or content gaps and their potential impact.

title: Data Quality: Consistency
description: The uniformity within the entire dataset or compared with similar data collections; for example, no changes in units or data types over time; item measured against itself or its counterpart in another dataset or database

title: Do the metadata indicate if all units have been translated into compatible forms?
description: E.g., Yes | No | Units are documented for compatibility | Script is provided to standardize | No units requiring standardization

title: Do any of the data follow a controlled vocabulary?
Is a reference provided for the controlled vocabulary used.
Describe any known consistency issues or steps taken to ensure consistency.
description: Include examples of standardization and any remaining inconsistencies.

title: Data Quality: Integrity
description: Provides verification that the data remains unchanged from the original; aka data fixity

title: Do metadata indicate if any quality assurance or peer review procedures been applied to the dataset?
description: E.g.: Internal quality control | External peer review | Automated validation scripts | Manual data checks | None

title: Do metadata describe the procedures used to ensure data integrity?
description: E.g.: Include use of checksums, version control, or audit trails to ensure data remains unchanged.

title: Does the dataset implement checksums?
description: Checksums provide completeness/component confirmation, e.g., checksum for a zip file or a list of image checksums to ensure downstream users get the expected data (sum-buddy can help with this).
